source_text: Aut si forte (quoniam aliter dogma tuum stare non potest) Adam ex se concepisse et peperisse responderis; Apostolum quidem non hoc sensisse nulli dubium; tu vero, quid sexui tuo volueris evenire, monstrabis.
pass_a_gloss: Or if perhaps (since your dogma cannot stand otherwise) you shall have answered that Adam conceived from himself and gave birth; that the Apostle indeed did not mean this is doubtful to none; but you will show what you wanted to happen to your own sex.
pass_b_english: Or perhaps, since your doctrine cannot stand otherwise, you will reply that Adam conceived and gave birth by himself. No one doubts that the apostle did not mean that. But you will show what you wanted to happen to your own sex.

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
